entries.title: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3
entries.jpTitle: 無職転生Ⅲ ～異世界行ったら本気だす～

review.en:
Episode #12: The End and the Beginning

"You could practically see the ゴゴゴ... rumbling in the background—that's how overwhelmingly tense it was. The exchange between the two of them... devastating, and not remotely satisfying or reassuring."

Seriously, what was with that tension? Twenty-three minutes consisting almost entirely of a conversation between the Rudeus of the future and the Rudeus of the present. It's been a long time since 23 minutes felt that short and that tense. And... it was scary.

Future Rudeus seemed to have mastered just about every kind of magic imaginable, and yet even he was completely powerless to do anything about what had happened. He came back with no regard whatsoever for his own life, just to deliver his bitter regrets and his warning. I don't know whether there was any hope left in what he was doing, but there is no question that this was the only thing he had left. The anguish and desperation behind his words came through with incredible force.

And then Sylphie and Roxy, concerned after hearing the noise but still somehow lacking any real sense of urgency, only made the whole thing feel even more ominous and intense. I did find it strange that Rudeus didn't tell them with an absolute, unmistakable "DO NOT" to stay out of the room and not eat anything, but I assume that was because he'd already resolved to handle it himself. And if he'd made too much of it, they might have tried to help him instead. They're also the two people who would probably pick up on just how serious Rudeus was without needing him to spell it all out.

But wow... all of a sudden, everything involving Hitogami—and really, everything involving the characters in this story—feels like it has started moving at once. It was almost too sudden, and yet at the same time the scope of what was covered was so enormous that I couldn't help thinking, "Really?"

Then there's the whole question of timelines—are there one or two?—and once you start thinking in terms of changing the past, the questions never end. Doesn't the mere fact that Future Rudeus came back already change what happens to Roxy and everything else? In any case, personally, there was a lot about this entire exchange that felt seriously strange to me.

He talked about Eris, Sylphie... and to some extent Nanahoshi, Cliff, the princess, Luke, and others. But what about his sisters, Zenith, Ruijerd, Perugius... and surely plenty of other people? And he never meets Orsted again after that? Not for decades? What about Nanahoshi? And more fundamentally, was Hitogami really unable to interfere with Future Rudeus coming back? When can he interfere, and when can't he? Did he deliberately allow it? Was even this visit part of his plan...? The more I think about it, the less I understand.

So as someone watching only the anime with absolutely zero knowledge of the source material, I assume there is much, much more going on behind all of this. Could Perugius actually be Rudeus too, somehow? Could Rudeus have existed for hundreds of years, or gone even further back into the past? There are all kinds of possibilities I can imagine, and I still can't shake my uneasiness about Future Rudeus and what we heard from him this episode.

Putting all of that aside, though, the tension, the performances, the direction, the structure... everything about this episode was incredible. There is no score other than an 11.

And there are only two episodes left...? What the hell is going to happen? I want to know what's in that diary, and surely Rudeus is going to tell Nanahoshi and his wives what he learned this time... Maybe that's as far as this cour will get.

And Eris... even if I've only heard half the story... this is way too complicated...

Seriously, just reunite already!
review.jp:
第12話: 終わりと始まり

"ゴゴゴ・・・という文字が見える程の圧倒的緊迫感、2人のやり取り、やり切れなくスッキリもしない"

『いや、何だこの緊迫感。ほぼ未来と現在のルディの会話だけの23分間。こんなに短く緊張した23分間は久しぶりだった。そして・・・怖い。想定しうるあらゆる魔法を身につけたと思える未来のルディがそれでもどうしようもなく、自らの命など顧みずに伝えに来たその無念と忠告。そこに希望はあったのかはわからないが、彼に残されていたのはもはやこれしかなかったことは間違いない。その悲痛な思いや訴えがとんでもなく伝わってきた。そして物音に気づき心配しながらもどこか緊張感のないシルフィとロキシーの姿・様子がまたその不気味さと強さの度合いを高める。ルディが2人に"絶対に"というような強さで部屋から出ないように、ものを食べないように言わなかったことに違和感も感じたが、それは自ら処理をする覚悟や考えがあってのことだろうし、そこまでやると逆に力になろうとしてくる・・・というのもあっただろう。また二人のことだからルディの真剣さを容易に感じ取れるということもあっただろう。いやいや・・・急にヒトガミに関わること、また本作の登場人物たちに関わることが一気に動き出したというか・・・。ちょっと唐突すぎて、またその割にカバーしている範囲が広すぎて・・・本当に?と思わずにはいられない。また世界線的に1つ、2つ?というのもあるし、過去改変という意味ではそもそも未来から来ただけでロキシーやその他に関わるの事象も変化しないの?とか考えたらキリがないが、いずれにしても個人的には相当な違和感を覚えるやり取りだった。エリスのこと、シルフィーのこと、、、多少ナナホシやクリフ、王女、ルークなどなどのこともいってたけど、妹たち、ゼニス、ルイジェルド、ペルギウス・・・などなど他にもいろいろあるだろうに・・・。そしてオルステッドともその後会うことがない?何十年も?ナナホシは?とか、そもそもそもそも、ヒトガミがこの未来ルディの来訪に関われなかったの?いつ介入できていつ出来ないの?わざと?とかも考えるとわからない。そもそもこの来訪すら計画の上?とか・・・。だから、アニメしてみていない原作知識０の私としては、裏にはもっともっといっぱいあるだろうし（ペルギウスも実はルディだとか?とか?ルディも何百年も存在していたりもっと過去にいっていたとか?）、この今回の未来のルディに対しての違和感も拭えずにいる。ただそうしたことは別にして、今回の話の緊張感や演技、演出、構成・・・全てが凄かった・・・11点以外ないだろう。そしてあと2話って・・・どうなんねん。日記の中身も気になるし、ルディは今回わかったことをナナホシや奥さんたちにも話すだろうし・・・今クールはそこまでかなぁ・・・。それにしてもエリス・・・話半分だけど・・・ややこしすぎる・・・。っていうか再会しよう!』

entries.title: Saga of Tanya the Evil II

review.en:
Episode #11: Hourglass

"I've never once considered myself a fan of this series, but when it delivers something on this level, all I can do is sing its praises—or perhaps simply stand in awe."

Stunning... There's really no other word for it. The animation and direction in particular were just... How much did they have to draw for this one episode? And how much thought went into deciding how to present it all? It was filled with one breathtaking shot after another. The carpet, the faces and expressions, the documents, the writing, the rain... I could go on forever.

And then there was the plot, the dialogue, and the way everything flowed. Degurechaff was at her absolute best here, but the exchanges between longtime friends Rudersdorf and Zettour were incredibly deep as well. Everything this cour has built up to this point, everything depicted in this episode, what we were shown in the first half, and then the direct conversation between the two of them—the arguments, agreement and trust, betrayal, scheming, and yet still feeling pain and agonizing over it all. Is that anguish even genuine? That question itself hangs over everything.

Degurechaff's position in all of this is fascinating. At times she's like a devil whispering in someone's ear, at times like some emotionless neutral presence, and at times simply one human being caught in the middle of it all... And yet Zettour himself says that he has lost his own humanity.

Rudersdorf surely has his own feelings about all of this as well. The betrayal and maneuvering are probably within the realm of what he anticipated...

Man... that was incredible.

Although, seriously, the Japanese is so difficult that I don't even understand half of it... What am I supposed to do with this?
review.jp:
第11話: 砂時計

"本作品のファンであったことは一度たりともないが、ここまでやられると絶賛するしかない、いや感嘆か"

『圧巻・・・としかいいようがない。特に作画、演出はもう・・・。この話のためにどれだけ描いたんだろう?そしてどう演出するか考えたのだろう?ため息の出るようなカットだらけだった。カーペット、顔・表情、文書、文字、雨、、、上げたらキリがない。そしてプロット、会話、またその流れ、デグレチャフの真骨頂でもあったが、また長年の親友ルーデルドルフとゼートゥーアの2人のやり取りも深かった。このクールでのこれまでの話で描いてきたこと、そしてこの話で描かれたこと、Aパートで見せたこと、そして2人の直接の会話、言い争い、同意と信頼、裏切り、策謀、それでも心を痛め悩む、それは本当の悩みなのか?という問い、デグレチャフの立ち位置はまるで悪魔の囁きのようで感情のない中立の存在のようであり、いち人間であるだけのようであり・・・。それに引き換えゼートゥーア自信は自身の人間性は失ったという・・・。そしてルーデルドルフにもきっと想うところはあるだろう。裏切りや画策などは想定の範囲内だろうし・・・。いやいや、凄かった。っていうか日本語が難しくてわからん・・・。困ったものだ。』

entries.title: You and I Are Polar Opposites Season 2

review.en:
Episode #11: A Place Where I Belong

"At this point, the way this show captures reality from so many angles and across so many layers is practically an art form. And Taira slowly, over all this time, coming to realize where he belongs."

Seriously, this is practically art in its own way. The raw realism of everyday life, with all these different situations, characters, and layers... It's unreal. By now, I'm sure most viewers have been completely drawn into that feeling of approaching the end of their final year of high school. And the way the show picks up on each individual character's thoughts, emotions, reactions, and actions within all of that is just insane.

And this time, after skipping over them last week and letting things simmer nicely, we return to Taira and Azuma... Taira is so twisted up in his own way that he somehow comes full circle and ends up throwing Azuma off instead, which is hilarious. But at the same time, everything he does makes perfect sense given the path he's taken to get here. And through all of that, there are things he's only been able to realize because of the time he's spent with everyone around him throughout his high school life. This time, that realization is about where he belongs.

That's why seeing Taira finally let go of everything that had been holding him back brings up this indescribable rush of emotion. And precisely because he's Taira, I still have my worries about what a future with Azuma might actually look like, but... we'll see where these two end up.

And then, ever so subtly, the episode weaves the main drama between Suzuki and Tani into all of this as well... And what exactly is going on with Tani? There was something very unusual about the way he was acting, and now I'm really curious about what that means...

Ahh, this is wonderful... Please don't end.
review.jp:
第11話: 居場所

"もはや芸術的なリアルな多角多層なシーンの切り取り、平のじっくりと時間を掛けた居場所への気づき"

『いやもうこれ、ある意味芸術的でしょ。この日常の生々しさ、それも状況、人物、レイヤーの数々・・・。あり得ん…今まさにあの高校3年生の終わりに向かっている状況に視聴者の大半が入り込んでことでしょう。またその中での個々のキャラの想い、感情、反応、行動の拾い方がエグい。そして今回は前回すっ飛ばしていい感じに寝かされた平と東・・・。平がネジ曲がってるもんで一周回って東を翻弄というのも笑えるし、でもそれは平にとってはこれまでの歩みから当然のことだし、その中で、自分がこの高校生活で周りのみんなと過ごしてきたからこそ気づくことの出来たことがあり、それが今回の自分の居場所。だからこそ吹っ切れた時の平の姿になんとも言えぬ想いが込み上げてくるのだろう。そんな平だからこそ、東との未来にはやはり不安もあるけど、果たしてどうなるんでしょうね。また、そこに微妙にメインの鈴木と谷のドラマを絡めてる・・・そしてあの谷の並々ならぬ様子の示すものとは?ってのも気になる・・・。あぁ素晴らしい・・・終わらないで。』

entries.romanized_title: Seihantai na Kimi to Boku 2nd Season
entries.synopsis: The second season of Seihantai na Kimi to Boku.

entries.title: Iron Wok Jan!

review.en:
Episode #11: A Bloody Baptism!

"More than anything, it's just so much fun to watch! It's exciting, the characters feel alive, and I can't take my eyes off it until the very end!"

Man, this is fun. Just like the spectators, the judges, the owner of Gobancho Restaurant, his fellow trainees, and even his opponents Kiriko and Célène, we have absolutely no idea what Jan is going to do next—and that's what makes it so much fun. It's fantastic. He's cocky as hell, he's bold, and he's just a blast to watch.

And then there are the pigeons... Will they become the pigeons of victory?

That outrageous dessert was great too... I love the furious reactions, the crowds surging forward, and the judges as well. Everything about it is just gloriously stupid—the best kind of stupid. And yet somehow, the food actually looks delicious enough that I want to try it.

So we know it's good, but what does it actually taste like? And what about Kiriko and Célène? Also, are there going to be multiple rounds in the final, like a third round or something?

Either way, as you'd expect, this show is entertaining me with a level of sheer insanity you almost never see these days.

Ahh, Jan is great.
review.jp:
第11話: 血の洗礼!

"とにかく見ていて楽しい!ワクワクするし、キャラが生きてるし、最後まで目がはなせません!"

『いやいや、面白い。見ているこちらも観客、審査員、また5番町飯店の店主、修行仲間だけでなく、対戦者のキリコとセレーヌ同様、ジャンが何をやるんだか、全くわからないし、楽しみだし、最高ですね。クソ舐めてるし、大胆だし、楽しい。そして鳩・・・勝利の鳩になるのでしょうか?それにしてもあの豪快なデザートも良かったな・・・。ブチギレたり押し寄せる観客もいいし、審査員もいい。とにかくアホ、気持ちの良いアホっぷり。でも不思議と美味しそうで食べてみたい。さて、美味しいということはわかったが、実際のお味はどんななんでしょう。そしてキリコとセリーヌは?また決勝戦には3回戦とかってあるのだろうか?いずれにしても当たり前ながら近年稀に見るぶっ飛び方で楽しませてもらってます。いいなぁジャン。』

entries.synopsis: Jan Akiyama, a cocky arrogant teenager wants to fulfill his grandfathers wish of defeating his arch nemesis Mutsuju Gobancho. When he arrives at the Gobancho restaurant he meets his granddaughter Kiriko Gobancho. Their rivalry is easily compared to Jan's and Kiriko's grandfathers, for Jan believes cooking is about competition and Kiriko believes cooking is about heart.

entries.title: Kaiju Girl Caramelise
entries.jpTitle: 乙女怪獣キャラメリゼ

review.en:
Episode #12: A Strike Filled with Love

"It's formulaic as hell, but I liked that it went all in and fully committed to it. Good for you, Chloe."

It's classic kaiju stuff mixed with the classic shy, cute girl story, but I liked it. Chloe finally breaking out of her shell and merging with Minami-kun. That's it. That's all I needed. Everything else? Who cares anymore.

Her mother? Her junior? The kaiju fanatic? Goriko? The idol? They're all just stage props there to make this one thing—the culmination of the love between these two—as grand and ridiculously over-the-top as possible.

I liked it.

Wouldn't recommend it, though.

Good stuff. I'm out.
review.jp:
第12話: この一撃に愛をこめて

"コテコテですが、極ふりしてやりきったのが良かった。クロエちゃんよかったね。"

『怪獣モノ、そして内気な可愛い女の子の定番ですが良かったです。もうクロエちゃんの脱皮と南くんとの融合。それだけ。後はもうどうでもいい。お母さん?その後輩?怪獣マニア?ゴリ子?アイドル?全部其れを壮大に大げさに見せる、2人の愛の結晶のための舞台装置。良かったです。オススメはしないけど。おつ。』

entries.synopsis:
Kuroe Akaishi just wants a normal high school life—but that’s impossible with a rare condition that turns her into a giant kaiju whenever her emotions spike! Things get even worse when she falls for Arata Minami, the most popular boy in class. Now every blush, heartbeat, and crush could trigger a monster transformation. Can Kuroe survive high school love before it destroys everything around her?!

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Draw This, Then Die!

review.en:
Episode #11: The Two of Us ~ Partners Who Complement Each Other Are Precious!

"That was just genuinely really good. There's even what feels like a pretty blatant homage in there, and I love how the two of them complement each other and become complete together."

Yeah, this was good... genuinely really good. Though I did feel it was a little lighter than usual.

Of course, Yasumin and Fujimori becoming a complete team by making up for what the other lacks is great, and there's something about the two of them that feels a bit like Manga Michi as well. I also liked how Teshima's memories of that awards ceremony in the past overlap with the two young girls standing in front of Shogakukan. And the way the two of them then end up having their work read by Teshima's former editor was really nice too.

Yeah... this was good.

I wonder how they're going to wrap everything up. Why has Teshima kept Yasumin's postcard all this time...? And he knew Yasumin was the one who sent it, right? So... what exactly does that mean?
review.jp:
第11話: ふたり~補いあえる仲間は尊い!

"普通に凄く面白かった、何となく思いっきりのオマージュもありのそれぞれが補い合いコンプするのもいい"

『いやいや、よかったですよ・・・、普通に凄く。ただいつもよりは少し軽めでもあったかな・・・とは思う。もちろんお互いに足りないところを補いあうことで完全体になるヤスミンと藤森もどこかまんが道的な感じもあっていいし、手島の過去の授賞式での思い出などが、若い二人が小学館を前にした時のものと被ったりするのもいい。そして2人が揃って手島の元担当編集の人に作品を読んでもらう流れも良かった。うん・・・良かったよ。どう締めるのかな?手島がなんでヤスミンのはがきをずっと持っているのか・・・それも差出人がヤスミンと知ってて?だよね。どういうことかな?』

entries.synopsis:
First-year high school student Ai Yasumi lives on the island of Izu Oshima and loves reading manga. But after a certain turning point, she sets her sights on creating stories of her own! As she dives into the world of manga-making, Ai faces challenges, growth, and the excitement of chasing her creative dreams. Where will her creative journey take her?

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Hell Mode: The Hardcore Gamer Dominates in Another World with Garbage Balancing Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 『ヘルモード　～やり込み好きのゲーマーは廃設定の異世界で無双する～』2nd Season

review.en:
Episode #12: Extra Skill

"We're finally approaching the climax, and things are really heating up. And even this late in the game, Yokohama Animation Lab is keeping the animation quality consistently solid. Good on them."

We're finally entering the climax... and even now, Yokohama Animation Lab's animation isn't falling apart. You can feel it from the OP and ED as well, but I can't help sensing how much love the production staff have for this series. It's the same feeling I got from Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho. Yeah... this is good. This is what makes anime so great.

Now the Hero has joined the fight, and while we're also shown the harsh reality facing Helena and the other character without an Extra Skill, the battle against the Demon God is underway. I also liked how they worked in the differences between Normal, Extra, and Hell Mode, and how the battle managed to feel genuinely exciting without resorting to the kind of excessive theatrics you'd expect from a certain weekly manga magazine.

The glimpses into the history between the elves and dark elves have me curious too, and I can't take my eyes off this now. What's going to happen next week? They can't even put up a fight at the moment...

Just please don't have everyone suddenly awaken some new power or something.

Actually, just give us another season or two already. I'd be more than happy with that.
review.jp:
第12話: エクストラスキル

"いよいよ架橋に差し掛かり盛り上がってきた、ここに来ても作画クオリティが安定のYAラボさん、偉い"

『いよいよ架橋・・・に入っても今の横浜アニメーションラボは作画が崩れない。そしてOPEDを見ても感じるが、制作の作品に対する愛を感じずにはいられない。これは、かの「鬼人幻燈抄」の時に感じたものだ。うん・・・いい、これだよね、アニメの良さって。さて、勇者も参加し、ヘレナやもう一人のエクストラスキル無しの現実を見せつつ魔神との対決。そこでまたノーマル・エクストラ・ヘルモードなどの解釈を交えたり、とある週刊マンガ雑誌系の過度な演出ではないアツさを感じさせる戦闘なども良かった。エルフとダークエルフの過去などにも興味が湧くし目が話せない。来週どうなる?全然手も足も出ないし・・・みんな急に覚醒、とかしないでね。っていうかもう1,2期やれよ。大歓迎だよ。』

entries.romanized_title: Hell Mode: Yarikomi-zuki no Gamer wa Haisettei no Isekai de Musou Suru 2nd Season
entries.synopsis: The second season of Hell Mode.

entries.title: Goodbye, Lara

review.en:
Episode #11: Witch Grace

"The fact that this is the most watchable episode yet, this late in the game, is probably because we're finally being shown what's actually happening and why. Rest in peace, Grace."

The animation really does keep getting better and more elaborate... This time, we get the story of Grace and her twin sister, the mother of Lala and her sister. We learn what Grace, a witch, used to be like... how she ended up the way she is now, and finally what her goal and true intentions are.

This is easily the most coherent the show has been so far, and more importantly, I can actually understand what the hell is going on while I'm watching it, so... yeah, I guess it was pretty good?

Of course, there are still plenty of things that bother me. Why exactly is Lala so special...? And the whole thing about the mermaid kingdom's source of energy—or whatever it is—being "true love," with humans somehow involved in all of that... feels pretty forced. Grace's relationship with Mari also feels tacked on, or like it's deliberately trying to squeeze tears out of us. And apparently humans are now the kind of people who immediately call mermaids monsters and kill them... There are plenty of things like that.

But this episode is really about Grace's life and how it comes to an end, so I'll mostly let those things slide... and consider the score a bit of a bonus for Grace.
review.jp:
第11話: 魔女グレイス

"ここに来て一番見れる回なのは、何があって何がどうしてるのかをやっと見せてるから、グレイスさん合掌"

『やはりドンドン作画が良くなるし凝ってくる・・・。今回はグレイスとララと姉の母親である双子の姉妹の話。魔女であるグレイスがかつては・・・そして何故今の姿になったのか、目的や真意も明らかになる。今までで一番ちゃんとしてるし、まず見てて何をやっているかが分かるから、まぁ良かったんじゃない?とは思う。でも、もちろん、なんでララが特別なのか・・・、そもそも人魚の国のエネルギー源?が真実の愛?で人間が・・・云々は無理やり臭いし・・・マリとの関係も取ってつけというかお涙頂戴というか、人は人魚をすぐ化物呼ばわりして殺すものになってるし・・・とかあるけど、今回はグレイスさんの生き様と終わりを見る回なのである程度流しつつ・・・のオマケの評価。』

entries.synopsis:
Once upon a time, a mermaid princess named Lara fell in love with a human prince. To be with him, she used a witch’s potion to become human—but the magic came at a cost: If she failed to find true love, she would vanish into sea foam forever. Now, 200 years later, Lara awakens in Lake Biwa with one final chance at life and love.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Dara-san of Reiwa

review.en:
Episode #12: Dara-san of the Reiwa Era

"We're finally approaching the endgame, but without getting too caught up in that, I'm simply enjoying this excellent show the same way I always have..."

Consistently excellent structure, direction, and storytelling. The people who thought of Dara-san, worshipped her, and tried to protect her in the past. And those feelings and traditions have been passed down for hundreds of years and still exist today. There's something fascinating about the way all of that has endured.

So many things seem to have changed without really changing at all—and yet, at the same time, they have changed...

The sequence leading up to that name they had been forbidden from remembering for so long was certainly effective as a dramatic climax. But this isn't really a show I want to judge based on those kinds of big dramatic moments, so I simply enjoyed what I always enjoy: the understated yet adorable relationship between these three, plus a few others around them.

Dara-san... seriously, what a good person.
review.jp:
第12話: 年末年始の過ごし方

"いよいよ大詰めだがそれとはそこまでかかわらずにいつものように秀逸な作品を楽しんでいる・・・"

『常に秀逸な構成、演出、ストーリーテリング。過去のダラさんを想う、祀る、守ろうとする、人たち。そしてそれは何百年も繋がって今もある。そのあり方の面白さ。それでも色々変わったようで変わって無くて、でも変わっていて・・・。その中でずっと思い出してはいけなかった名前を・・・の流れは盛り上がりとしては良いとは思ったが、本作をそういった盛り上がりで評価を同行とは思わないので、単純にいつものように淡々としつつも愛らしい3人+αの関係を楽しみました。ダラさん・・・マジでいいひと。』

entries.synopsis:

entries.title: A Livid Lady's Guide to Getting Even: How I Crushed My Homeland with My Mighty Grimoires
entries.jpTitle: ブチ切れ令嬢は報復を誓いました。 ～魔導書の力で祖国を叩き潰します～

review.en:
Episode #11: Itsuwari no Kinka

"The story, its setup, and its structure aren't bad in themselves, but I can't shake the feeling that they don't really come together with the series as a whole."

This is actually a surprisingly well-constructed story, and it's reasonably engaging to watch. But that's largely because of the setup, the tricks, and the various gimmicks involved. Do any of those things actually make the series itself—or, by extension, its characters—more compelling? In other words, if you asked me whether this particular story really had to be told with this series and these characters, I don't think I'd say yes.

Elisabeth's utterly ruthless, brutal, no-holds-barred retaliation—mentally cornering her enemies and effectively destroying them socially—and the surprisingly well-thought-out economic punishment feel somewhat disconnected from each other to me.

After all, I still don't understand why Elisabeth is so incredibly capable in the first place—and the same goes for her subordinates. The prince being an idiot is basically just part of the setup, and then there's the cutesy girl cozying up to him... I don't know, the whole thing just leaves me wondering what I'm supposed to make of it.

So yeah, it's surprisingly coherent and perfectly watchable, but an 8 is about as high as I can go.
review.jp:
第11話: 偽りの金貨

"話や仕掛け、構造自体は悪くない、だがそれが作品と一体感を欠いている気がしてならない"

『意外とよく出来てる話ではあるし、ある程度見応えがあるものではある。ただこれは、設定、仕掛け、ギミックによるもので、それがこの作品、ひいては登場人物に対する魅力などに繋がっているの?つまり、この話は、この作品やキャラたちでなければならないか?と言われればそんな風には思えない。このエリザベートの徹底的で残忍でブレーキのない暴力による報復っぷり、精神的に追い詰め社会的な抹殺、と意外とよく出来た経済的な制裁は分離して感じられるかな。なにせ、何故このエリザベートがそんなに有能なのかわからんし（部下もだけど）、王子の馬鹿さも設定、そこい取り入るぶりっ子女とかもね・・・難でしょうって感じだから。なので意外とちゃんとしてて見れるけど8点がせいぜい。』

entries.romanized_title: Buchigire Reijou wa Houfuku wo Chikaimashita.: Madousho no Chikara de Sokoku wo Tataki Tsubushimasu
entries.synopsis:
Elizabeth Leiston, daughter of the influential prime minister, is a picture-perfect lady on the path to becoming the future queen of the Kingdom of Haldoria. But her life takes a sudden turn for the worst when her fiancé makes a show of publicly calling off their engagement. Soon after, he throws her in jail and starts spreading nasty rumors about her. The encouragement Elizabeth receives from her loyal waiting maid, Mireille, and her inner fury are all she needs to reconsider her goals. Why should she continue devoting herself to a country that doesn’t respect her when she can trample over it instead? She will get even with those who wronged her and bring down the damned kingdom, even if it’s the last thing she does! Luckily, Elizabeth is no damsel in distress and has seven powerful magic grimoires she won’t hesitate to use. Get ready because this ruthless lady is out for blood!

(Source: J-Novel Club)

entries.title: Ascendance of a Bookworm Season 3
entries.jpTitle: 本好きの下剋上　領主の養女

review.en:
Episode #22: Wilfried's Actions

"Instant and utterly lacking in any appeal. What a disappointing result."

Awful. Wilfried is just way too stupid. And this has been the case ever since that aunt of his showed up. His involvement with her was already poorly handled, barely anything was depicted afterward, and now we're simply told that he was thoroughly deceived and manipulated. We don't even get to see his conversation with his imprisoned aunt—or whoever she is—and then he suddenly shows up to blame Ferdinand and Myne?

And then, as if they needed to hastily throw in some reason for Myne to want to help him even a little, we suddenly get this setup where Myne gets all excited about having a little sister who adores her and calls her "Big Sister~," and apparently she just wants to look good in front of her?

That's just way too stupid.

It honestly scares me that I'm starting to feel like I don't even want to watch a series I once loved anymore—or rather, I'm amazed that this production company has actually managed to make me feel that way.

The OP and ED are awful too...

What are they even trying to do with this?
review.jp:
第22話: ヴィルフリートの行い

"インスタント、何の魅力もない、残念な結果"

『酷い。ヴィルフリートが馬鹿すぎるだけ。それは例の叔母が出てきた時からで、その関わりも微妙、その後も対して描かず、今回もただひたすら騙され誘導されたということ、そして幽閉されてる叔母?との会話も描かず、突然フェルディナンドとマインを責めに来る?そしてさもマインがそれを少しでも救おうとする根拠として今回急遽登場して配置され、自信が"お姉さまぁ~"と慕われる設定に萌えだすマインが、ただただ妹に良い顔見せたい?って・・・それ、アホ過ぎる。かつて大好きだった作品を、もう見たくもないとすら思い始める自分が怖い、というかそう思わせることに成功しているこの制作会社が・・・。OPEDも酷いしなぁ・・・、何がやりたいの?』

entries.romanized_title: Honzuki no Gekokujou: Ryoushu no Youjo
entries.synopsis:
Following a disastrous encounter with a noble, Myne finally resolves to say goodbye to her family and friends in the lower city, changing her name to “Rozemyne” and beginning her new life as the adopted daughter of Ehrenfest’s archduke. However, her days as an archnoble in noble society are brutal, as she is put through rigorous etiquette and magic training on top of her duties as High Bishop and forewoman. It all proves too much for a weak little seven-year-old girl... Or it would have, had the High Priest not offered her the keys to the temple’s book room as a reward. If she could get her hands on those, she’d be able to read all sorts of precious books! Her name may have changed, but Rozemyne’s passion for books remains the same as she charges into a whole new world! The detailed setting expands as the printing industry grows in size. Here begins Part 3 of this biblio-fantasy for book lovers everywhere!

(Source: J-Novel Club)

entries.title: The World Is Dancing
entries.jpTitle: ワールド イズ ダンシング

review.en:
Episode #12: The World Is Dancing

"What the hell was this? Give me back the 12 episodes I spent on this cour... So he grew physically, struggled with it, went back home, and found some comfort. Good for him."

Seriously? What the hell was this...?

Wait, that spiky-haired kid from the Southern Court... Kogane? Was he dead? I guess I misunderstood that... Good grief, this is hard to follow.

So Kiyasha is going through puberty and growing pains, his voice is changing, and it's all very difficult for him? Then he went back home and found some comfort? Good for him, I guess.

I should've listened to that voice in my head around episode two or three that was already screaming, "Yeah, this isn't gonna work." Even after that, there were plenty of times when I thought, "I can't do this anymore..."—like when they started throwing jazz and whatever else into a story set during the time of Ashikaga Yoshimitsu.

So at the very least, let me offer a few words of appreciation to myself and every other viewer who pointlessly stuck it out to the end:

"Thanks for making it through. Good work."
review.jp:
第12話: ワールドイズダンシング

"何すかこれ?1クール12話返せ・・・。身体的に成長して悩んで実家帰って癒されてよかったですね"

『マジで?ナニコレ・・・?っていうかあのツンツン頭の?南朝の子…コガネ?は死んでたの?ちょっと勘違いしてました…。トホホ、分かりづらい。鬼夜叉は第2次性徴と成長痛で声も変わって大変なの?実家帰って癒されたの?良かったね、って感じです。もう2,3話くらいの時点で強烈に思った、"これダメだわ"という心の声に従ってればよかった。その後も、足利義満の時代の舞台にジャズやら何やらを使うとかって時とかにも、何度も"もう無理・・・"って思ったのにね。せめて無駄に完走した自分や他の視聴者にねぎらいを「お疲れ様でした、ご苦労さまでした」。』

entries.synopsis:
Born into a life of acting and dance with a traveling theater troupe in 14th-century Japan, 12-year old Oniyasha has one problem—he doesn't know what the point of any of it is. "Why must I step with the left foot here instead of the right? Why is one performance good and another, bad? Why do people dance at all?" It all seems perfectly arbitrary, until a chance encounter in a run-down shack sets him down a path to revolutionizing the art form and influencing much of Japanese culture to come. A fictionalized account of the early life of Zeami Motokiyo (Oniyasha), the founder of modern Noh theater—the world's oldest surviving theater art—this coming-of-age artist's journey vividly brings to life a man far ahead of his time during one of Japan's most culturally and socially vibrant eras.

(Source: Kodansha Comics)
